newsitem.title: Italy: Italy declares state of emergency over Albanians.
newsitem.headline: Italy declares state of emergency over Albanians.

text.p: Italy declared a national "state of emergency" on Wednesday, recognising that it had been overwhelmed by a flood of well over 10,000 refugees from Albania's turmoil in less than a week.
The emergency, which will remain in force until June 30, allows access to 61 billion lire ($36 million) the government said it had earmarked to cover assistance to the refugees.

A special cabinet meeting also decided that genuine refugees would be allowed to stay in Italy for no more than three months and said Albanians "deemed to be a danger to public security" would be forcibly repatriated, a government statement said.

Interior Ministry Giorgio Napolitano said 289 "undesirables" had already been flown in three giant Chinook army helicopters from the southeastern port of Brindisi to Albania's capital Tirana, where they were handed over to Albanian police.

He said the exodus had brought 10,619 people across the Adriatic in a ramshackle fleet of boats between March 13 and seven a.m. (0600 GMT) on Wednesday -- three times the number Italy had prepared to receive when the unrest erupted.

Nearly 300 more arrivals, many of them women and children soaked to the skin, reached Brindisi on Wednesday on two Italian coastguard vessels sent to rescue them from a stricken tug that had run out of steam 20 miles off the Albanian coast.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, has been rocked by unrest since the collapse in January of shady "get-rich-quick" savings schemes. The protests mushroomed this month into armed rebellion in the south and chaos has spread across the country.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said a European Union plan to help Albania restore order and provide emergency relief was intended to favour a peaceful, political end to the chaos.
"It is also designed to ease the flow of refugees, whose consequences concern not only Italy but all of Europe," a government statement quoted Dini as telling the cabinet.
Police sources, quoted by ANSA news agency, said security had been increased at the Ventimiglia frontier post with France to try to stop Albanians heading into northern Europe.
The German Interior Ministry also said it had instructed border guards to increase surveillance for Albanians at frontier posts.
Italy's centre-left government acted amid growing pressure from overburdened local authorities in the southeast and from the opposition to ensure that refugees stayed no longer than necessary.
Napolitano told parliament that Albanians would be carefully screened to ensure they were genuinely in need of protection.

Only those who were "the most exposed to dangers" in Albania would be allowed to stay in Italy for a temporary period. Permits would be issued for up to 60 days, renewable for a maximum of an additional 30, Napolitano added.

Italy faced a severe crisis in 1991 when some 40,000 Albanians commandeered rusting freighters and poured across the Adriatic after the collapse of 45 years of Stalinist rule in the hope of jobs and wealth in Italy and elsewhere in Europe.
The country has since grappled with continuing problems of illegal Albanian immigration and drugs and arms-smuggling.
Several escaped prisoners from jails stormed in Albania's unrest and suspected mobsters have used the latest exodus to slip into Italy, according to ministers.
Italy also says racketeers in the Albanian port of Durres have hijacked the exodus, charging desperate emigrants up to $600 each for a place on a boat to a new life abroad.
